To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of blockchain in the IoT can provide the following advantages: security, trustworthiness, scalability, and interoperability.
the IEEE P193.1.1 ROO standard is the first Internet standard for IoT that can benefit from the use of blockchain.

blockchain technology can be successfully applied to the IEEE 1932.1 standard, with the caveat that the current state of blockchain technology and the ROOF standard is not sufficient for a successful deployment.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) the definition of the architectural framework that can be used for the deployment of blockchain technology in ROOF; (2) the definition of a blockchain implementation that can be used to implement the ROOF framework and (3) the definition of an evaluation methodology for the blockchain implementation that can also be applied to other blockchain implementations in the future.
the use of blockchain in the IEEE 19 31.1 ROOF standard and its impact on the IoT.
the use of blockchain within the IEEE P19311.1 ROOF standard, and the results of this research will be used to define and refine the ROOF standard.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
blockchain technology can be a key component for the IEEE 193.1.1 ROO standard and, in general, for federated IoT systems.
blockchain technology is a key enabler to the IEEE 193.1 standard, but it still has some critical issues that need to be addressed to ensure its effective deployment in the IoT.
blockchain is a key enabler for the IEEE P19311.1 WG to accomplish its goals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IEEE 193.1 standard is a great opportunity for the IoT community to exploit the potential of blockchain technology in a real-world application.
the IEEE P1932.1 WG is working on a new standard for the IoT that is based on a blockchain architecture.
the IEEE 1932.1 WG is working on a standard to facilitate IoT interoperability in a decentralized manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while blockchain technology can be a valuable asset in the IoT domain, the current state of the technology is not mature enough to be deployed in real-world applications.
blockchain technology is not a magic solution that will solve all the problems in the IoT.
blockchain technology can play a pivotal role in enabling the IoT and in particular in enabling the ROOF standard.
